author: reek
body: The test that would have caught it. `poll-key` used to answer named keys with DOM key codes while answering characters with ASCII, and DOM key codes land on printable characters, so Up and shift+7 were both 38 and Right and the apostrophe were both 39. Every existing keyboard test typed one side or the other. None typed both, so the suite could not express the failure, and the contract prose stated both halves of the collision on adjacent lines without anybody seeing it.

author: reek
body: The timeline types each colliding pair back to back: shift+7 then Up, then the apostrophe then Right, then `t` then F5. Each pair must come back as two DIFFERENT values, and the character half must be the CCE code point of that character rather than a number this test made up.
